sentences.text: Gongshuilong is distinguished by uniquely elongated, backward-curved neural spines on its tail vertebrae that created a tall, sail-like structure. These spines were 8.5 times taller than the vertebrae's central body.

Fossils were found in March 2021 during construction in Shahe, Ganzhou city, Jiangxi Province, China. Han Yao and colleagues formally described the new genus and species Gongshuilong fanwei in 2026. The species name fanwei refers to the dinosaur's prominent sail-like tail morphology.
The genus contains only one species, G. fanwei, known from a bonebed containing at least two individuals.
Phylogenetic analysis recovered Gongshuilong as a member of the tribe Brachylophosaurini within the clade Saurolophinae.
This animal lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) in China, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago. It is the first named hadrosaurid discovered in South China.
The exact evolutionary relationships within the Brachylophosaurini tribe remain unresolved, with Gongshuilong forming a polytomy with Wulagasaurus, Acristavus, and other North American genera.
